environment.note: Fresh scheduled-session sandbox, no GPU (no nvidia-smi binary present), torch==2.5.1+cpu via scripts/setup_dev_env.sh, Python 3.12.
environment.not_committed: .venv/ and outputs/ are gitignored; not part of this commit.

investigation.summary: Both the control and canvas arms of the first cycle of a newly started scheduled continuous loop (continuous-openui-local-20260804) finalized all 3/3 smoke records inside a typed decode timeout (decode_timeout_document_count=3, document_n=3, completed_document_n=0), so smoke.structural_similarity and every other smoke quality metric came back null and the primary metric was unavailable -- an infrastructure measurement_incomplete signal, not a model result. scoreboard.json's evaluation_policy.decode_timeout_seconds is 8.0 (per-record, screening role default from climb_policy.decode_timeout_seconds_for_role), and suites.smoke.effective_decode_timeout_seconds_max/min is 24.0 -- consistent with decode_batch_size_max=3, decode_chunk_n=1 (all 3 records decoded as a single batched chunk, so the per-chunk alarm is 8.0s x 3 records = 24.0s total, not 24.0s per record).
investigation.new_evidence_this_cycle: The continuous-loop status matrix's decode telemetry (compiler_ms_mean) for both arms lands at ~23.2s (23251.2ms control, 23169.1ms canvas) -- i.e. grammar-constrained compiler-tree compilation alone (evaluation_policy.compiler_decode_mode=tree, strict_compiler_tree), before any token decode, already consumes essentially the entire 24.0s chunk budget on this CPU-only sandbox. This is a more specific data point than the c5 finding (autotrain-cycle-c5-dual-arm-decode-timeout-unresolved.md), which did not distinguish between seed-dependent worst-case decode behavior (hypothesis a) and CPU-throughput-vs-wall-budget headroom (hypothesis b) -- this cycle's compiler_ms_mean measurement is direct support for hypothesis (b) in this sandbox, though it does not rule out (a) contributing in other sandboxes/seeds.
investigation.root_cause: unresolved as a fix: strict_compiler_tree grammar-constrained compilation is measured taking ~23s/record on this CPU-only sandbox's hardware, which alone exceeds the 8.0s per-record screening decode-timeout budget used to size the chunk alarm. Whether this is inherent to the compiler-tree path on CPU without acceleration, or specific to this fixture/model config, was not isolated further this cycle.
investigation.not_a_fix: No code change was made. `_effective_record_decode_timeout` (src/slm_training/harnesses/model_build/eval_runner.py:1187) and `_fit_screening_decode_timeout_seconds` (scripts/run_autotrain_continuous.py:261) were both read and are already covered by existing tests (test_eval_wall_fairly_caps_each_remaining_record; test_replayed_dual_arm_timeouts_remain_inconclusive_and_require_repair, which intentionally locks in that a symmetric both-arm decode timeout must stay climb_state=inconclusive and keep demanding repair_harness rather than silently retiring to a new hypothesis). Per the finding autotrain-harness-incomplete-not-invalid-20260803.md, this is filed as an infrastructure incomplete, not a model result, and is retryable after a harness fix -- not a reason to weaken the decode-timeout wall-clock contract to force gates green (that path was already tried and reverted for the c5 campaign for contradicting the tested contract).
investigation.recommended_next_step: Let the driver's built-in frozen-replay handling replay the identical frozen arm (retry_measurement, already queued in cycle_handoff.json and not gated on repair_harness per continuous.md's execution/steering-action exemption) on the next cycle of this loop to test whether the timeout reproduces. If it reproduces again, that is two consecutive cycles of the same class of dual-arm decode timeout in this specific CPU-only sandbox type (distinct from the c5 campaign, a different loop/session/day) -- route to improve-openui-harnesses for dedicated compiler-tree decode profiling (e.g. a per-phase compiler_ms breakdown, or evaluating whether decode_batch_size_max should default lower than 3 on CPU so a single slow record cannot exhaust the whole chunk's alarm budget for its batch-mates) rather than raising decode_timeout_seconds blind.

next_priority: replay the identical frozen control/canvas arms (retry_measurement, queued); if reproduced, hand off to improve-openui-harnesses for compiler-tree decode profiling on CPU-only sandboxes
